gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-khojki: Noto Serif Khojki reads soft and literary, with short ascenders over big bowls. Amadeus stretches wide and bold above it, so give the serif body a little extra size to let its gradual weight change show.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-lao: Noto Serif Lao brings a big lowercase against its capitals, its bowls shifting gently in weight, bookish and authoritative. Amadeus commands with thread-like strokes; the body does the subtle, steady talking.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-makasar: Amadeus stretches its words wide, with generous gaps where curves meet stems. Noto Serif Makasar is editorial and dignified, its strokes stepping softly from heavy to light beneath a towering x-height.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-malayal: Cut sharp and stretched wide, Amadeus keeps a single cutting width throughout. Noto Serif Malayalam supplies the standout quality: big open counters plus gently thinning bowls, refined and bookish.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-np-hmon: Noto Serif NP Hmong reads soft and literary, lightly shaded like worn charcoal. Amadeus has no shading to guide the eye, but across paragraphs the body feels textured and refined.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-old-uyg: Noto Serif Old Uyghur has tall bowls like blown glass bulbs and quiet stroke contrast. Noto Serif Old Uyghur keeps a refined, literary hush over many lines, its arches thinning slowly, while Amadeus skims along bold.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-oriya: Wide and bold, Amadeus has an outline you could follow with a finger. Noto Serif Oriya sits between monoline and razor-thin hairlines, giving that outline an authoritative, dignified partner.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-ottoman: Dignified is the mood here: Noto Serif Ottoman Siyaq swells only slightly in its bowls, with a sizable lowercase body. Amadeus hits first, built like bent tubing of one gauge.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-sinhala: Amadeus stretches wide and bold, its strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle, above the tall letter band of Noto Serif Sinhala. Give the serif body a touch more size so its restrained strokes show.
gen-dafont-amadeus-gf-noto-serif-telugu: Amadeus stretches its words wide, and its diagonals carry the same heft as the stems. And Noto Serif Telugu, traditional and refined, moves with gentle shifts in weight, so the bold heading feels sharper beside it.
